plain.text: Abram returned from Egypt to Canaan, very rich in livestock, silver and gold. Lot, travelling with him, also had flocks and herds and tents. The land could not support them both, and their herders began to quarrel. Abram said to Lot, "Let's not have any quarrelling between us, for we are family. Is not the whole land before you? Let's part company. If you go left, I'll go right; if you go right, I'll go left."

Lot looked and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the LORD. So he chose the Jordan plain and set out east, pitching his tents near Sodom. But the people of Sodom were very wicked and sinned greatly against the LORD.

After Lot left, the LORD said to Abram, "Look around from where you are: north, south, east and west. All the land you see I will give to you and your offspring forever. I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth." Abram moved his tents to the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, and built an altar to the LORD there.

summary.bigIdea: Abram chooses peace over winning, and God renews his great promise.
points: Abram and Lot's herders quarrel, and Abram generously lets Lot choose first.
Lot chooses the rich plain near wicked Sodom.
God promises Abram the land and countless descendants.
summary.reflection: Abram let Lot choose first to keep the peace. Where could you choose generosity over getting your own way?
